summary: A 35-foot Aermotor steel fire tower on Loon Lake Mountain, erected in 1917 and NRHP-listed in 2008; unused since 1971 and not restored, though the hike is popular.

facts.design: 35-foot steel-frame Aermotor fire lookout tower with cab, on the Loon Lake Mountain summit
facts.status_note: Standing but unrestored with its stairs removed; the 2018 visit found poor condition (windows, wood, paint)

access.note: Stairs removed to keep people from climbing; DEC says the tower has not been restored. The hiking trail itself is popular.

visit.trail_note: At the March 2018 visit the trail was well marked and the lot was plowed; active logging may have been under way nearby.

evidence.quote: One of the early lookouts in the state, erected in 1917, and reconstructed in 1927 after it was blown down by a hurricane, Loon Lake Mountain Fire Tower is again a popular hiking destination since the NY DEC rebuilt the trail in 2013.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the tower was reconstructed in 1927 after a hurricane. Wikipedia says the 1917 tower replaced a 1912 wooden tower and does not mention 1927. Unresolved; the story presents 1927 as the register's claim.
A 2007 comment says the main trail access crossed private land; the 2018 visit describes a signed trail and a plowed lot. The story follows the 2018 description.

notes_for_editor: The 1917 erection is consistent across NHLR, Wikipedia and NPGallery metadata. The 1927 hurricane rebuild appears only in NHLR. The NRHP nomination PDF is marked not yet digitized, so Wikipedia's 1912 wooden predecessor could not be checked at source. Current condition rests on the 2018 NHLR visit and an undated DEC page; no visit after 2018 was found.
